Compute and interpret SE = σ/√n and explain why n quadrupling halves it.
Interpret a 95% interval as a property of the procedure, not a probability about a fixed parameter.

title: Journey 6: Hypothesis testing: evidence under a null model
summary: A test compares an observed statistic with the distribution it would have under H₀. The p-value is a tail area conditional on that model; α is chosen before the data; failing to reject is not accepting.
keywords: If the null were true, how unusual is what we observed — and what decision follows?
Write H₀ and Hₐ and choose a sidedness before looking at the result.
Read a p-value as P(statistic at least as extreme | H₀), never P(H₀ true).
Distinguish Type I from Type II error and statistical from practical significance.

title: Journey 7: Experimental design: earning a causal claim
summary: Randomization, control, blinding and a pre-specified outcome are the design features that make groups comparable. The A/B test is one randomized design, not the definition of all experiments.
keywords: What has to be true about the design before a difference can support a causal sentence?
Identify treatment, control, response and the unit of assignment.
Explain what randomization balances in expectation — and what it does not guarantee.
Distinguish single-blind, double-blind and open-label designs without overclaiming.

title: Journey 8: Relationships and causality: what r can and cannot say
summary: Pearson r measures the strength and direction of a linear association. It is not a slope, it can be near zero under a strong curve, and observational co-movement is not a causal effect.
keywords: Is the association linear, could a third variable explain it, and what would a causal claim require?
Read a scatterplot before trusting a correlation coefficient.
Explain why r ≈ 0 does not rule out a strong non-linear relationship.
Separate correlation, regression slope and a causal effect in plain language.

title: Journey 9: Synthesis: choose, check, decide, explain
summary: The final journey turns the reference into a decision aid: a connected mental model, a formula workbench, a tool navigator, misconception cards, the checkout case and a printable field guide.
keywords: Given a new question, which tool applies — and what would make the answer irresponsible?
Route a new question to a defensible method and name its assumptions.
Use the formula sheet without detaching a formula from its conditions.
Tell the checkout story end to end with consistent denominators and honest uncertainty.

title: 1. The big picture: what is statistics?
summary: “A statistic is the same thing as a parameter.” A statistic is computed from a sample and varies; a parameter describes the population and is usually unknown.
keywords: Name the six stages from data to decision and say what each one produces.
Use population, sample, parameter and statistic correctly in one sentence.

title: 2. Data types and what they permit
summary: “If it is written with digits, it is numerical.” Customer IDs and phone numbers are labels; averaging them is meaningless.
keywords: Sort observations into numerical (discrete/continuous) and categorical (nominal/ordinal).
Explain why a numeric-looking identifier is categorical and why ordinal ranks are not measurements.

title: 3. Descriptive vs inferential statistics
summary: “A sample summary is already a conclusion about the population.” Description stops at the data; inference adds a model, uncertainty and assumptions.
keywords: Tell a statement about the observed sample from a claim about the wider population.
Identify which branch a question belongs to before computing anything.

title: 4. Measures of center
summary: “The mean is always the best centre.” In a skewed distribution or with outliers, the mean is pulled toward the tail and may stop representing a typical value.
keywords: Compute mean, median and mode and explain when each is the better summary.
Predict which of mean and median moves further when one extreme value is added.

title: 5. Measures of spread
summary: “Standard deviation and standard error are interchangeable.” SD describes individual values; SE describes how a statistic varies across repeated samples.
keywords: Distinguish range, variance, standard deviation and IQR by what they measure and their units.
Explain the n−1 sample denominator and the 1.5×IQR outlier rule.

title: 6. Probability, complements, independence and conditionals
summary: “Independent means the events cannot happen together.” Independence is about information: knowing B does not change P(A). Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together at all.
keywords: Compute P(Aᶜ), P(A∩B), P(A∪B) and P(A|B) from a sample space.
Explain why two mutually exclusive events with positive probability cannot be independent.

title: 7. Probability distributions: mass vs density
summary: “The height of the normal curve is the probability of that value.” Height is density; probability is area under the curve between two values.
keywords: Read a PMF bar as a probability and a PDF area as a probability.
State why the probability of one exact value under a continuous distribution is zero.

title: 8. The binomial distribution
summary: “Binomial counts how many trials happen.” It counts successes among a fixed number of trials; the number of trials is an input, not the outcome.
keywords: Check the fixed-n, independent-trial, constant-p, binary-outcome conditions.
Compute P(X=k), a lower tail or an upper tail and read E(X)=np and Var(X)=np(1−p).

title: 9. The normal distribution and z-scores
summary: “Changing σ changes the total probability.” The total area stays 1; a larger σ flattens and widens the curve.
keywords: Locate a value on a normal curve and shade the corresponding area.
Standardize with z=(x−μ)/σ and apply the 68–95–99.7 rule as an approximation.

title: 10. The Poisson distribution
summary: “λ=20 means P(X=20) is high, so 20 is the mode.” λ is a mean count; at integer λ the mode is actually the pair λ−1 and λ.
keywords: Define λ as the mean count per fixed interval and compute exact and tail probabilities.
Verify E(X)=Var(X)=λ and explain the discrete support.

title: 11. The central limit theorem
summary: “The CLT says the data become normal once n is large.” It is the sampling distribution of the mean that approaches normality, not the population or a single sample.
keywords: Explain that the distribution of sample means tends toward normality under stated conditions.
Show that the mean of the sampling distribution equals μ.

title: 12. Sampling distribution
summary: “A sampling distribution is just a bigger sample.” It is the distribution of a statistic over repeated samples — a different object with a different axis.
keywords: Distinguish the population distribution, one sample's distribution and the sampling distribution.
Label each panel with its own unit and axis.

title: 13. Standard error
summary: “SE is the SD of the data divided by √n because the data got narrower.” The data distribution did not change; the sampling distribution of the mean did.
keywords: Compute SE = σ/√n and its estimated form s/√n.
Explain why SE shrinks as n grows while the SD of the values stays put.

title: 14. Confidence intervals
summary: “There is a 95% probability that the fixed parameter is inside this interval.” Once computed, the interval either covers the fixed parameter or does not; 95% is the long-run coverage of the method.
keywords: Build estimate ± critical value × SE and explain each term.
Interpret 95% coverage as a property of repeated procedures.

title: 15. Hypothesis testing and the two hypotheses
summary: “The test calculates the probability that H₀ is true.” It calculates the probability of data at least this extreme assuming H₀ is true.
keywords: Write a null and an alternative for a comparison, including sidedness.
Explain why the null is a model to test, not a belief to prove.

title: 16. The hypothesis-testing workflow
summary: “The workflow starts with a p-value.” It starts with the question, the populations and the hypotheses; the statistic comes later.
keywords: Order the seven stages from populations to a qualified conclusion.
Identify the decision point where α enters.

title: 17. Sampling variability inside a test
summary: “A difference between sample means proves a difference between populations.” Samples vary; the test asks whether the observed difference is unusual under H₀.
keywords: Show that two samples can differ even when the population means are equal.
Reframe the question as whether the difference is larger than sampling noise.

title: 18. Test statistic and standard error
summary: “A test statistic of 3.6 is a 3.6% probability.” It is a distance in SE units; the probability comes from the null distribution, not from the number itself.
keywords: Express a test statistic as a distance measured in standard errors.
Reproduce (5.4 − 0)/1.5 = 3.6 and explain what the 3.6 means.

title: 19. The p-value
summary: “The p-value is the overlap between the null and alternative curves.” It is a tail area of the null sampling distribution, not an overlap.
keywords: Define a p-value conditional on H₀ and the chosen sidedness.
Distinguish the p-value area from an overlap between two distributions.

title: 20. The significance level α
summary: “α is the probability that the result is wrong.” α is the long-run false-positive rate under H₀ for the chosen rule.
keywords: Explain α as a pre-declared Type I error rate and decision threshold.
Show why moving α after seeing p changes the rule, not the evidence.

title: 21. The decision rule
summary: “Failing to reject proves H₀.” Absence of sufficient evidence against H₀ is not evidence that H₀ is exactly true.
keywords: Apply p ≤ α → reject H₀ and p > α → fail to reject H₀.
Avoid the phrase “accept H₀” and explain the boundary case p = α.

title: 22. Type I and Type II errors
summary: “Type I and Type II errors are complements.” They are conditional on different states of reality; α + β is not 1 in general.
keywords: Map the four reality × decision cells and name the two errors.
Relate α to Type I error and β to Type II error under a specified alternative.

title: 23. Statistical vs practical significance
summary: “Statistically significant means important.” Significance is about compatibility with H₀; importance depends on effect size, context and cost.
keywords: Separate evidence against H₀ from the size and business value of an effect.
Explain how a huge sample can make a trivial difference significant.

title: 24. Experiments
summary: “Any comparison is an experiment.” Without manipulation and a design that controls alternatives, it is an observational comparison.
keywords: Identify the treatment and the response in a causal question.
Explain what manipulating the treatment buys over observing it.

title: 25. Controlled experiments
summary: “Control means do nothing.” A control can receive a placebo or the current standard, and the point is a comparable reference.
keywords: Describe the role of a treatment group and a control group.
Explain why imbalance on a covariate can create a misleading difference.

title: 26. Randomization
summary: “Randomization guarantees the groups are balanced.” It balances in expectation; any one run can still be imbalanced.
keywords: Explaining randomization as a design device, not a data-cleaning step.
Show balance in expectation and finite-sample imbalance in a seeded shuffle.

title: 27. Blinding and placebo
summary: “Double-blind means the analyst also does not know the hypothesis.” It means participants and the people administering or assessing treatment do not know assignment.
keywords: Distinguish participant blinding, experimenter blinding and double blinding.
Explain what a placebo controls and what blinding cannot fix.

title: 28. RCT vs A/B testing
summary: “A/B testing and RCTs are unrelated.” An A/B test is a randomized controlled experiment applied to a product change.
keywords: Explain that an A/B test is a two-arm randomized design, not the definition of an RCT.

title: 29. Independent and dependent variables
summary: “Whatever is on the X axis causes the Y.” Axis placement is a convention; only the design supports a causal reading.
keywords: Map the predictor/treatment to X and the response to Y in a scenario.
Explain why the role is defined by the question, not by the axis label.

title: 30. Correlation and Pearson r
summary: “r is the slope.” r is standardized covariance; the slope depends on the units of X and Y and is not bounded by 1.
keywords: Read direction and linear strength from r and from the scatterplot.
Explain why r is unitless and bounded in [−1, 1].

title: 31. Pearson correlation and linear relationships
summary: “r ≈ 0 means no relationship.” It means no *linear* relationship; a U-shape or cycle can be strongly dependent.
keywords: Show that a strong curved pattern can produce r near zero.
Restrict Pearson interpretation to linear association.

title: 32. Correlation is not causation
summary: “A high r proves X causes Y.” Association is compatible with reverse causation, confounding and coincidence.
keywords: Separate co-movement from a causal effect.
Name the alternative explanations that an observational r cannot exclude.

title: 33. Confounding variables
summary: “If the correlation is strong, a confounder cannot explain it.” A strong pooled association can be entirely produced or reversed by a third variable.
keywords: Draw a third-variable structure Z→X, Z→Y and explain the induced association.
Show what happens to a pooled correlation after within-group separation.

title: 34. Correlation vs experiment
summary: “A correlation study can establish causality if the sample is big enough.” Sample size narrows uncertainty; it does not remove confounding.
keywords: Choose the tool based on the question's evidential target.
Explain why a randomized experiment supports a stronger causal claim than an association.

title: 35. Correlation vs regression
summary: “r=0.8 means Y rises 0.8 units per unit of X.” That is a slope statement; r has no units.
keywords: Read a regression slope with units and compare it with r.
Show that positive affine rescaling changes the slope but not r.

title: 36. How the topics connect
summary: “The topics are independent chapters.” Each later method depends on the sampling and probability ideas built earlier.
keywords: Trace the prerequisite path from description to decision.
Locate a concept in the atlas and open its source section.

title: 37. The formula index
summary: “The formula is the method.” A formula without its assumptions and data requirements is not a valid analysis.
keywords: Match each formula to the question it answers and the conditions it requires.
Read every symbol and unit without detaching it from its section.

title: 38. Decision rules: when the question changes
summary: “The most advanced method is the safest.” The right method is the one whose assumptions the data and design can support.
keywords: Route a new question to a starting method and name its alternatives.
See which inputs and assumptions the method requires before it is used.

title: 39. The mistakes to avoid
summary: “Memorising the wrong sentence is enough to avoid it.” Each myth needs a concrete counterexample and a corrected sentence.
keywords: Recognise the ten misconceptions and the counterexample that defeats each.
Use the correction without hiding the original claim.

title: 40. The end-to-end checkout case
summary: “A significant lift is automatically worth shipping.” The decision also needs effect size, cost, risk and a pre-specified meaningful threshold.
keywords: Carry one scenario from question through assignment, data, test, decision and business interpretation.
Keep denominators and uncertainty consistent across every panel.

title: 41. Final mental model
summary: “A decision is just the p-value.” The decision combines evidence, uncertainty, effect size, cost and context.
keywords: Describe the layered system from population to decision in one pass.
Say where uncertainty, confounding and assumptions enter.

title: 42. One-page cheat sheet
summary: “A cheat sheet is a substitute for the lesson.” It is an index back to the lesson and its qualifications.
keywords: Use a compact, printable field guide without losing the conditions.
Scan the formula, the question and the caution together.

title: 43. Course conclusion
summary: “The final answer is a number.” The final answer is a qualified decision with an explicit limitation.
keywords: Run the transferable process: question → design → data → method → evidence → decision.
Name the limitation that would change the conclusion.

title: Sample mean
summary: Formulas
keywords: x-bar equals the sum of x sub i from i equals one to n, divided by n.

title: Sample variance
summary: Formulas
keywords: s squared equals the sum of squared deviations from x-bar, divided by n minus one.

title: Population variance
summary: Formulas
keywords: sigma squared equals the sum of squared deviations from mu, divided by capital N.

title: Standard deviation
summary: Formulas
keywords: Standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

title: Interquartile range
summary: Formulas
keywords: IQR equals the third quartile minus the first quartile.

title: Complement rule
summary: Formulas
keywords: The probability of A complement equals one minus the probability of A.

title: Independence
summary: Formulas
keywords: A and B are independent exactly when the probability of both equals the product of their probabilities.

title: Conditional probability
summary: Formulas
keywords: The probability of A given B equals the probability of A and B divided by the probability of B.

title: Binomial PMF
summary: Formulas
keywords: The probability of exactly k successes in n trials is n choose k times p to the k times one minus p to the n minus k.

title: Binomial mean and variance
summary: Formulas
keywords: The expected number of successes is n p and its variance is n p times one minus p.

title: Normal density
summary: Formulas
keywords: The normal density at x is one over sigma root two pi, times e to the negative x minus mu squared over two sigma squared.

title: Z-score
summary: Formulas
keywords: z equals x minus mu, divided by sigma.

title: Poisson PMF
summary: Formulas
keywords: The probability of k events is e to the negative lambda times lambda to the k, divided by k factorial.

title: Poisson mean, variance and SD
summary: Formulas
keywords: The mean and variance are both lambda, and the standard deviation is the square root of lambda.

title: Mean of the sampling distribution
summary: Formulas
keywords: The expected value of the sample mean is the population mean mu.

title: Standard error of the mean
summary: Formulas
keywords: The standard error of the sample mean equals sigma divided by the square root of n.

title: Estimated standard error
summary: Formulas
keywords: The estimated standard error of the mean is approximately s divided by the square root of n.

title: Confidence interval
summary: Formulas
keywords: A confidence interval is the estimate plus or minus a critical value times the standard error.

title: Test statistic
summary: Formulas
keywords: The test statistic is the observed value minus the hypothesized value, divided by the standard error.

title: p-value
summary: Formulas
keywords: p = P(result at least as extreme | H₀ true)
The p-value is the probability of a result at least as extreme as the observed one, given that the null hypothesis is true.

title: Decision rule
summary: Formulas
keywords: p ≤ α → reject H₀; p > α → fail to reject H₀
Reject the null when p is less than or equal to alpha; fail to reject it when p is greater than alpha.

title: Simple linear regression
summary: Formulas
keywords: Y equals beta zero plus beta one times X.

title: Pearson correlation (extension)
summary: Formulas
keywords: r equals the sum of products of deviations, divided by the square root of the product of the sums of squares.

title: Slope and correlation (extension)
summary: Formulas
keywords: The fitted slope equals r times the standard deviation of y divided by the standard deviation of x.

title: Population
summary: Glossary
keywords: The complete set of units a question is about. Its summary is a parameter.

title: Sample
summary: Glossary
keywords: A subset of the population that is actually observed. Its summary is a statistic.

title: Parameter
summary: Glossary
keywords: A fixed, usually unknown population quantity such as μ or σ.

title: Statistic
summary: Glossary
keywords: A quantity computed from sample data, such as x̄ or s; it varies from sample to sample.

title: Descriptive statistics
summary: Glossary
keywords: Summaries of the observed data, with no claim beyond those observations.

title: Inferential statistics
summary: Glossary
keywords: Generalising from a sample to a population using a model and quantified uncertainty.

title: Mean
summary: Glossary
keywords: The sum of values divided by n. Sensitive to outliers.

title: Median
summary: Glossary
keywords: The middle value after sorting; resistant to outliers.

title: Mode
summary: Glossary
keywords: The most frequent value; there may be several modes or none.

title: Standard deviation
summary: Glossary
keywords: The square root of variance, in the original units; spread of individual values.

title: IQR
summary: Glossary
keywords: Q₃ − Q₁, the range of the middle 50% of the data; resistant to outliers.

title: Outlier
summary: Glossary
keywords: A value unusually far from the bulk of the data; in a box plot, beyond 1.5×IQR fences.

title: Complement
summary: Glossary
keywords: The event that A does not occur: P(Aᶜ)=1−P(A).

title: Conditional probability
summary: Glossary
keywords: P(A|B), the probability of A after restricting the sample space to B.

title: Independence
summary: Glossary
keywords: Knowing one event occurred does not change the probability of the other: P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B).

title: Mutually exclusive
summary: Glossary
keywords: Events that cannot occur together, so P(A∩B)=0. Not the same as independent.

title: PMF
summary: Glossary
keywords: A discrete probability mass function: each value has a probability, and the masses sum to 1.

title: PDF
summary: Glossary
keywords: A continuous density: probability is area under the curve, and a single point has probability zero.

title: Binomial distribution
summary: Glossary
keywords: The count of successes in n independent trials with constant success probability p.

title: Normal distribution
summary: Glossary
keywords: A symmetric continuous bell curve defined by μ and σ, with total area 1.

title: Z-score
summary: Glossary
keywords: z=(x−μ)/σ, the signed number of standard deviations from the mean.

title: Empirical rule
summary: Glossary
keywords: For a roughly normal distribution, about 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 SD of the mean.

title: Poisson distribution
summary: Glossary
keywords: A count distribution for events in a fixed interval with mean λ; mean equals variance.

title: Lambda (λ)
summary: Glossary
keywords: The Poisson mean count per stated interval — a rate, not a probability.

title: Central limit theorem
summary: Glossary
keywords: Under suitable conditions, the sampling distribution of the mean approaches normality as n grows.

title: Sampling distribution
summary: Glossary
keywords: The distribution of a statistic over repeated samples of the same size from the same population.

title: Standard error
summary: Glossary
keywords: The standard deviation of a statistic's sampling distribution; for the mean, σ/√n.

title: Confidence interval
summary: Glossary
keywords: An interval produced by a procedure with a stated long-run coverage rate.

title: Coverage
summary: Glossary
keywords: The long-run proportion of intervals from a procedure that contain the fixed parameter.

title: Null hypothesis
summary: Glossary
keywords: The model of no difference or no effect used to derive the null sampling distribution.

title: Alternative hypothesis
summary: Glossary
keywords: The claim being assessed; its direction determines what counts as more extreme.

title: Test statistic
summary: Glossary
keywords: A standardized distance between the observed result and the value expected under H₀.

title: p-value
summary: Glossary
keywords: P(statistic at least as extreme as observed | H₀ true). Not P(H₀ true).

title: Alpha (α)
summary: Glossary
keywords: The pre-declared Type I error threshold; reject H₀ when p≤α.

title: Type I error
summary: Glossary
keywords: Rejecting a true H₀ — a false positive, with rate α under the null.

title: Type II error
summary: Glossary
keywords: Failing to reject a false H₀ — a false negative, with rate β under a specified alternative.

title: Power
summary: Glossary
keywords: 1−β: the probability of rejecting H₀ when a specified alternative is true.

title: Practical significance
summary: Glossary
keywords: Whether an effect is large enough to matter in context, independent of statistical detectability.

title: Randomization
summary: Glossary
keywords: Assigning units to conditions by a random mechanism so groups balance in expectation.

title: Blinding
summary: Glossary
keywords: Withholding treatment assignment from participants and/or assessors to reduce expectation effects.

title: RCT
summary: Glossary
keywords: A controlled experiment that assigns units randomly to treatment conditions.

title: A/B test
summary: Glossary
keywords: A two-arm randomized experiment comparing a control (A) with a treatment (B).

title: Confounder
summary: Glossary
keywords: A third variable that affects both X and Y and can create or distort an observed association.

title: Pearson r
summary: Glossary
keywords: A unitless measure of the direction and strength of linear association, in [−1,1].

title: Regression slope
summary: Glossary
keywords: The expected change in Y per one-unit increase in X, in the units of the data.

title: Absolute lift
summary: Glossary
keywords: p_B−p_A in percentage points; the raw difference between two rates.

title: Relative lift
summary: Glossary
keywords: (p_B−p_A)/p_A; the difference as a proportion of the baseline rate.

title: The mean is always the best measure of centre.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Use the median when the distribution is skewed or outliers matter to the question.
In [2,4,4,4,5,5,7,100] the mean jumps above 16 while the median stays at 4.5. One value changes the typical picture.

title: Standard deviation and standard error are the same thing.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: SD = spread of observations; SE = spread of a statistic across repeated samples.
The SD describes individual values and stays roughly fixed as n grows; SE=σ/√n shrinks because it describes the sample mean.

title: A p-value is the probability that H₀ is true.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Read it as a compatibility check with the null model, never as the posterior probability of the null.
The p-value is computed *assuming* H₀. It is P(data at least this extreme | H₀), not P(H₀ | data).

title: The p-value is the overlap between the null and alternative distributions.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Shade the equally-or-more-extreme region under H₀; do not shade the alternative.
Overlap involves both distributions; the p-value uses only the null sampling distribution and the observed statistic's tail.

title: If p > α, we accept H₀.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Say “fail to reject H₀” and describe the uncertainty and the alternative explanations.
A non-significant result means the data are compatible with H₀ at this threshold; it does not establish that H₀ is exactly true.

title: You can choose α after seeing the p-value.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Declare α, the test and the sidedness before looking at the data.
Choosing the threshold after the result changes the rule and inflates the false-positive rate. α is part of the design, fixed before analysis.

title: Statistically significant means practically important.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Report the effect size and its interval against a pre-specified meaningful threshold.
With a large enough n, a 0.01-percentage-point difference can produce p<0.05 while being commercially irrelevant.

title: r ≈ 0 means X and Y are unrelated.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Look at the scatterplot; r measures linear association only.
A symmetric U-shape has strong dependence but r near 0, because positive and negative linear contributions cancel.

title: A strong correlation proves causation.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Causal claims need design — random assignment, control, or another credible identification strategy.
Ice-cream sales and drowning correlate because both follow temperature. A third variable can create the association without either causing the other.

title: r=0.8 means Y increases by 0.8 units when X increases by one unit.
summary: Misconceptions
keywords: Report the slope with units separately from r.
r is unitless and bounded by ±1; the slope is r·sᵧ/sₓ and changes when the units of X or Y change.

title: Randomization makes the two groups identical.

title: Which clause filters individual rows before grouping happens?

title: In a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders, which rows are guaranteed to appear in the result?
summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: A LEFT JOIN preserves the left table. Customers without orders appear once with NULLs in the order columns.

title: Which of these are aggregate functions? Select all that apply.
summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: COUNT, SUM, and AVG collapse many rows into one value. ROW_NUMBER is a window function and returns a value per row.

title: You want only regions whose total sales exceed 1,000,000. Where does that condition belong?
summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: The condition depends on an aggregate (SUM), so it must run after grouping. That is HAVING's job.

summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: A CROSS JOIN produces the Cartesian product: 3 rows × 2 rows = 6 rows.

title: In standard SQL, the expression NULL = NULL evaluates to TRUE.
summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: Comparisons with NULL produce UNKNOWN, not TRUE. Use IS NULL or IS NOT DISTINCT FROM to test for NULL.

title: Which expression numbers employees 1, 2, 3… within each department by descending salary?
summary: SQL · SQL for Analysts
keywords: PARTITION BY restarts the numbering per department, and ORDER BY salary DESC defines the sequence. Without PARTITION BY

title: Which statement returns exactly one row per group?
